title: Kinshasa hospital workers’ strike over appointment authority at the Hôpital général de référence
organizer: The hospital intersyndical called the strike; Zoom Eco describes the Feb 18 courtyard action by hospital employees without naming a separate organizer.
participants_original: Hospital employees, including doctors, nurses and administrative staff (no count reported).
threshold_50_evidence: A courtyard gathering by hospital employees is reported, but no count or minimum is given; >=50 remains unverified.

start_date.summary: Zoom Eco dates the courtyard action to the afternoon of Feb 18; Radio Okapi says the strike started Thursday last week in its Feb 24 article.

end_date.summary: No end date is reported in the article.

location.summary: The action concerns the Hôpital général de référence de Kinshasa in Kinshasa.

organizer.summary: Radio Okapi attributes the strike call to the intersyndical; Zoom Eco describes employees acting in the courtyard without naming a separate protest organizer.

demands.summary: Union representatives ask the President to resolve the appointment dispute between the national health ministry and the provincial government.

participants_original.summary: Zoom Eco names doctors, nurses and administrative staff among the employees, but publishes no count.

participants_min.summary: No numeric minimum can be established.

participants_max.summary: No numeric maximum can be established.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: A courtyard gathering is reported; no attendance estimate or numeric minimum is given.

protester_violence.summary: Zoom Eco reports that employees burned tires; the codebook threshold for protester violence is unavailable, so the coded value remains unknown.

state_response.summary: No response to the Feb 18 gathering is established. Police/military actions described by Zoom Eco relate to the broader prior dispute, so they are not coded as a response to this gathering.

notes: Candidate retained because reporting documents a labor action and a public courtyard gathering with demands about a state appointment dispute. Attendance is unreported, so the >=50 threshold remains unresolved. Zoom Eco reports tire burning, but whether this meets the project violence code requires reviewer judgment under the unavailable original manual. Radio Okapi says the strike continued as of Feb 24; the end date remains unknown. The reported Feb 18 start is supported by contemporaneous reporting.
open_questions: How many workers gathered in the courtyard?
When did the strike end or change form?
Does tire burning satisfy the project’s protester-violence code?
Are the Radio Okapi and Zoom Eco accounts independent reports or linked through an unrecorded origin?

title: Kindu youth march demanding the resignation of Governor Auguy Musafiri
threshold_50_evidence: Unknown. The article describes a youth march but reports no crowd count or minimum.

start_date.summary: The report is dated Feb 8 and says the march took place that Monday.

end_date.summary: The police dispersed the march on Feb 8 after the memorandum was deposited.

location.summary: The march and courthouse are in Kindu, the provincial capital of Maniema.

organizer.summary: The article identifies the participants as youths but names no group.

demands.summary: The memorandum called for applying the law in the governor’s case and for his resignation following reinstatement.

participants_original.summary: The article refers to young participants, without a numeric estimate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No crowd count or minimum appears in the report; threshold remains unknown.

protester_violence.summary: The article does not report protester violence.

state_response.summary: The report says police dispatched by the city hall dispersed the march; it also says protesters deposited their memorandum shortly before dispersal. Other response dimensions are unreported.

notes: The report links the march to the Constitutional Court reinstating a governor who faced provincial assembly proceedings. Depositing the memorandum is coded as accommodation of the submission only, not acceptance of the demand or victory. Crowd threshold is not established.
open_questions: Were at least 50 people present?
Did any other source report arrests, injuries or violence?
What became of the resignation demand and pending proceeding?

title: Union Sacrée-affiliated parties’ Kananga march demanding gubernatorial elections
organizer: Political parties and associations identifying with the Union Sacrée de la Nation, including UDPS/Tshisekedi, UNC, RDT, Congo Positif and UNAFEC.
participants_original: About 5,000 according to organizers; 3,000 according to police.
threshold_50_evidence: The article reports both a police estimate of 3,000 and organizer estimate of about 5,000; each is far above 50.

start_date.summary: Actualite.cd dates the march to Saturday 27 February 2021.

end_date.summary: The article describes the march route and memorandum deposit but does not state a physical end time.

location.summary: The march took place in Kananga, Kasaï Central.

organizer.summary: The action was organized under the banner of parties and associations affiliated with the Union Sacrée de la Nation; the article names several.

demands.summary: A memorandum addressed to the prime minister asks the CENI to organize gubernatorial and deputy-gubernatorial elections; it also asks President Tshisekedi to intervene.

participants_min.summary: The lower published estimate is 3,000 from police.

participants_max.summary: The upper published estimate is about 5,000 from organizers.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Both reported estimates exceed 50 by a wide margin.

protester_violence.summary: The source explicitly describes the march as peaceful and reports no contrary protester violence.

state_response.summary: Police are described as escorting the march; the article does not establish a response to the election demand or subsequent action on the memorandum. All seven response dimensions remain unknown.

notes: This is a public march making an electoral-process demand to national officials. It is coded as process/election advocacy rather than support-only mobilization. Depositing the memo at the CENI office is not treated as a substantive government response. A separate Actu30 lead about ECIDE/Fayulu supporters marching in Kananga (S010) has not been linked to this event; verify dates and story lineage before any merger or independence claim.
open_questions: Was the memorandum subsequently answered or acted on?
When did the physical march conclude?
The Feb 10 ECIDE march (S010) is separately dated and differently organized; is there evidence that the Feb 10 and Feb 27 actions belong to a wider campaign? Do not merge their separate assemblies.

title: ECIDE Kananga march for local official resignations and governor elections
location: Notre Dame roundabout and streets of Kananga, Kasaï Central
organizer: ECIDE Kasaï Central federation; the article names its federal president Élie Mputu as march initiator.
participants_original: Unreported; three ECIDE members are reported arrested, and other participants reportedly fled. The arrest count is not a crowd count.
threshold_50_evidence: The article establishes a planned public march and police dispersal at the meeting point, but reports no total crowd estimate. Three arrests do not establish 50 participants.

start_date.summary: Article body says the march occurred Wednesday 10 February 2021; metadata publication time is also 10 February.

end_date.summary: Police stopped the march at its starting point; the article does not state when any dispersal or related activity ended.

location.summary: The march and gathering began at Notre Dame roundabout in Kananga.

organizer.summary: ECIDE’s Kasaï Central federation organized the march; its federal chair Élie Mputu is named as initiator.

demands.summary: The party demanded resignations of the mayor and urban police commander over insecurity, and elections for a new provincial governor; the memo was addressed to the President.

participants_original.summary: No crowd count; the report says the ECIDE chair and two militants were arrested and the others fled.

participants_min.summary: No total crowd minimum can be derived from three named detainees.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Public march reported but turnout is not quantified; the threshold remains unresolved.

protester_violence.summary: No protester violence is described; silence does not establish no_explicit.

state_response.summary: Police prevented the march and dispersed it at the starting-point roundabout; the federal ECIDE leader and two militants were arrested. The article gives no evidence of beatings, shootings, killings, accommodation or official inaction.

notes: The Actu30 article was unavailable through the web reader’s cache but was read over ordinary public HTTPS after a fresh receipt and full manual host/story review; temporary response body was removed. This is distinct by date and organizer from the Feb 27 Union Sacrée election-process march (E003). The similar S011 Coulisses result may concern the same Feb 10 action, but its source relationship is unresolved; neither is counted as independent confirmation.
open_questions: What was the total turnout, and did it reach 50?
Did the police use a specific method of force beyond stopping the action and making arrests?
Is S011 another account of the same Feb 10 action, and does it reveal additional threshold or response evidence?

title: Kananga judicial defenders’ march against the new bar law
location: TGI to the Provincial Assembly via MONUSCO headquarters, Kananga
organizer: Judicial defenders attached to Kananga’s Tribunal de grande instance; their union is represented in the article by Me Crispin Kamba.
participants_original: Judicial defenders; no count or estimate reported.
threshold_50_evidence: An organized public march is reported, but the article gives no attendance count; >=50 remains unresolved.

start_date.summary: Infocongo dates the march to Thursday 25 February 2021.

end_date.summary: The article describes the march and memo deposit but does not give a physical end time.

location.summary: The procession left the Kananga TGI and ended at the provincial assembly after passing MONUSCO headquarters.

organizer.summary: Judicial defenders attached to the TGI organized the march; Me Crispin Kamba is identified as speaking for their union.

demands.summary: They opposed the bar law as reducing defenders’ rights and asked the President to seek a constitutional review.

participants_original.summary: Participants are identified as judicial defenders; no number is supplied.

participants_min.summary: No numeric minimum can be determined.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: A public march is documented, but the crowd size is unreported.

protester_violence.summary: The article explicitly characterizes the march as peaceful and describes no protester violence.

state_response.summary: The provincial assembly quaestor received the memo and promised to forward it to the appropriate authority; no arrests, force or later substantive action is reported.

notes: A Radio Okapi archive result lists a same-day report with a matching headline, but no direct story URL or written origin relation was found; the archive is not counted as corroboration. Infocongo alone confirms the march and the assembly quaestor’s receipt/forwarding promise. The memo reached an official but did not establish a substantive policy concession.
open_questions: Did at least 50 people attend?
Was the Radio Okapi article the same story, a republication, or a separate account?
Was the memo forwarded or did the President/Court act on it?

title: Lucha Kananga march demanding the mayor’s departure over insecurity
organizer: Lucha, identified by both reports as the citizen movement in the street.
participants_original: Lucha demonstrators; Actualite.cd reports two injured militants but neither outlet reports a turnout count.
threshold_50_evidence: Neither report supplies an attendance estimate or numerical minimum. Two injured militants are not a crowd count; >=50 remains unverified.

start_date.summary: Actualite.cd dates its report to 12 February and describes the Lucha march that day; InfosLive URL path is dated 12 February and says “this Friday.” The event date is retained as 12 February.

end_date.summary: Neither report states a physical end time or date. Police prevention of the banned march does not establish when the overall action ended.

location.summary: Both reports place the Lucha street action in Kananga, Kasaï Central; no exact route is reported.

organizer.summary: Both reports identify Lucha as participating in the Kananga street action.

demands.summary: InfosLive says Lucha demanded the mayor’s resignation for incompetence and lack of strategy; the Actualite.cd article quotes a Lucha spokesperson demanding “exiger le départ du maire de Kananga.” The target is the local DRC city mayor, not a foreign official or support-only target.

participants_original.summary: Both reports describe Lucha demonstrators; Actualite.cd names two seriously injured militants but gives no attendance estimate.

participants_min.summary: No numeric minimum of total participants is reported; two injured people do not establish one.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Neither source provides a crowd count or numerical minimum. Two reported injuries cannot be used as turnout; the >=50 threshold remains pending.

protester_violence.summary: Police alleged that some Lucha militants threw stones and injured police, while activists described a peaceful march and the injuries as caused by police bayonets. The competing claims are unresolved; protester violence remains unknown.

state_response.summary: InfosLive gives no response to Lucha. Actualite.cd reports that police prevented the march under a mayoral ban, supporting crowd_dispersal=yes. A Lucha account attributes two injuries to police bayonets; police denies this and offers a competing account. Beatings and injury causation remain unknown; no arrests, shootings, killings or accommodation are established.

notes: Two outlets describe the same Feb 12 Kananga Lucha action; S028 is a separate Actualite.cd report, not a second event. The mayoral resignation/departure demand is explicit. Attendance remains unreported. Actualite.cd reports two serious injuries and competing accounts: Lucha attributes injuries to police bayonets and police denies this, says it prevented the mayor-banned march, and alleges stone-throwing by militants. Crowd dispersal is coded yes from the explicit prevention account; arrests, beatings, protester violence, physical end and injury causation remain unresolved. S013 may relate to this event or the distinct announced civic-forces march.
open_questions: Did at least 50 people participate?
Does S013 describe this Lucha action, the separately announced civic-forces march, a related account or a different event?
What can independent evidence establish about the competing activist and police accounts of injuries and protester conduct?
When did the physical action end?
